channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: US Says Ramaphosa Letter Fails to Meet Its Demands, BD Reports
item.description: A letter written by South African President Cyril Ramaphosa to his US counterpart failed to sway Washington over its demands that Pretoria alter policies aimed at redressing apartheid-era inequalities, Business Day reported, citing US Ambassador Leo Brent Bozell III.
item.dc:creator: Arijit Ghosh

item.title: UK Borrowing Overshoots Forecasts in Budget Setback for Healey
item.description: Britain borrowed more than forecast in the first five months of the fiscal year, piling fresh pressure on Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey ahead of his debut budget next month.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Atkinson and Philip Aldrick

item.title: Trump to Meet Ukraine's Zelenskyy
item.description: US President Donald Trump will meet Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Tuesday. The Ukrainian relationship with the US has faced new strains in recent days with Trump demanding Zelenskyy stop targeting oil refineries in Russia. Bloomberg's Oliver Crook breaks down the situation. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: UK to Give Saudi Arabia Defensive Support to Counter Houthis
item.description: The UK has agreed to support Saudi Arabia’s military in countering the Houthis, as the kingdom comes under frequent attack from the Iran-backed militants. Refueling of Saudi jets on missions that the UK considers defensive will begin in the coming days, and the operation is expected to last weeks. The decision represents one of Andy Burnham’s first significant military decisions since becoming prime minister in July. Bloomberg's Stuart Livingstone-Wallace reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US, China Talks Focus on Trade, AI, Investment
item.description: US and Chinese officials discussed artificial intelligence, investment and trade during a second day of talks in New York on Monday. The focus is on whether the two nations can agree on extending a trade truce set to expire in November, and how long any new agreement could last. Bloomberg's Stephen Engle reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: The Mishal Husain Show Live From Singapore
item.description: Former Singapore Foreign Minister George Yeo and former United Nations Security Council President Kishore Mahbubani join Mishal Husain to analyze our increasingly multipolar world. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Unions Are Pushing Into UK Firms After Employment Rules Change
item.description: Trade unions are increasingly pushing to get a seat at the table in UK workplaces, after the Labour government relaxed collective bargaining rules earlier this year.
item.dc:creator: Irina Anghel

item.title: India, Central Europe Seek Closer Ties as US Relations Strain
item.description: India’s Foreign Minister S Jaishankar met four Central European counterparts to boost cooperation and deepen defense ties as New Delhi broadens its diplomatic outreach at a time of strained relations with the US.
item.dc:creator: Unni Krishnan

item.title: Canada Seeks to Wrap India Trade Talks Soon as US Ties Fray
item.description: Canada’s trade minister said trade talks with India are “moving along really well” and could conclude in the coming months, as his country looks for new markets for its goods amid a tariff war with the US.
item.dc:creator: Shruti Srivastava

item.title: China, EU Should Avoid Trade Clash, Beijing’s Top Diplomat Says
item.description: China and the EU should find a way to avoid a confrontation over trade, Foreign Minister Wang Yi said — comments that come as a deadline to find solutions to the two sides’ differences approaches.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Pentagon Blacklist Lingers as Irritant in Trump-Xi Talks on AI
item.description: The US government’s increased reliance on a Pentagon blacklist to target China’s biggest companies threatens to cast a pall over President Donald Trump’s summit this week with his Chinese counterpart, Xi Jinping.
item.dc:creator: Kate O'Keeffe

item.title: China and US Discuss AI, Investment on Second Day of Trade Talks
item.description: Chinese and US officials wrapped up their second day of talks in New York on Monday to discuss artificial intelligence, investment and trade as they sought to advance negotiations ahead of President Xi Jinping’s visit to the US this week.
item.dc:creator: Nectar Gan

item.title: Trump, Mamdani Meet Ahead of UN General Assembly
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Rep. Darrell Issa (R-CA), Vice Chairman of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, says he opposes a diesel export ban, but warns US oil producers against using higher global prices to boost profits while creating scarcity at home. Frank Cilluffo, Director of the McCrary Institute for Cyber and Critical Infrastructure Security at Auburn University, says the US will “never firewall” its way out of the cyber threat and needs to take more proactive steps against adversaries. Jozef Síkela, EU International Partnership Commissioner, says Europe is already the largest contributor to development assistance and is looking to mobilize more private capital for emerging and developing markets. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Vietnam Leader Says US Deal Close, Denies Re-Routing China Goods
item.description: Vietnamese President To Lam said his nation is “very close” to a trade deal with the US as he pledged to buy more high-tech goods like aircraft to narrow the trade gap ahead of talks with Trump administration officials in New York.
item.dc:creator: Francesca Stevens, Nguyen Dieu Tu Uyen, Nguyen Xuan Quynh and Haslinda Amin

item.title: Síkela Says Europe Looks to Expand Development Financing
item.description: Jozef Síkela, EU International Partnership Commissioner, says Europe is already the largest contributor to development assistance and is looking to mobilize more private capital for emerging and developing markets. Síkela says the EU’s partnership package with Greenland is aimed at strengthening security and resilience while creating jobs and economic value. Síkela says Europe wants to work with Canada to reduce critical-mineral dependence on China. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Cilluffo Warns Cyber Attackers Still Hold the Advantage in AI Era
item.description: Frank Cilluffo, Director of the McCrary Institute for Cyber and Critical Infrastructure Security at Auburn University, says the US will “never firewall” its way out of the cyber threat and needs to take more proactive steps against adversaries. Cilluffo says AI can strengthen defenders but warns that, for the foreseeable future, the initiative remains with attackers. Cilluffo also argues the US must keep human control over increasingly powerful AI systems while continuing to compete with China. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Kallas Urges EU to Bolster Red Sea Mission Against Houthi Threat
item.description: The European Union’s top diplomat, Kaja Kallas, called for member states to send more naval vessels to protect commercial shipping in the Red Sea.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Palasciano

item.title: Rep. Issa Warns Oil Companies Against Profiting From US Shortage
item.description: Rep. Darrell Issa (R-CA), Vice Chairman of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, says he opposes a diesel export ban, but warns US oil producers against using higher global prices to boost profits while creating scarcity at home. Rep. Issa calls the gains a “tremendous windfall,” and companies “can’t have it both ways.” Rep. Issa argues the US has mismanaged the Houthi threat for years, allowing the group to rebuild its capabilities and support attacks in the region. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump, Mamdani Set Barbs Aside for ‘Productive’ Meeting on NYC
item.description: President Donald Trump and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani capped a face-to-face meeting with a surprise joint appearance before reporters in which both played up what has become one of the more unlikely relationships in US politics.
item.dc:creator: Cameron Fozi and Myles Miller

item.title: Hungarian PM Rejects Report on Ukraine Joint Fuel Reserve
item.description: Hungary won’t be building a joint strategic fuel reserve with Ukraine, Prime Minister Peter Magyar said, as he blamed the head of the country’s oil company for keeping him out of the loop on the project.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Escritt
